topic: Bharat Heavy Machinery: Functional Silos & Inter-Departmental Conflict
questionText:
Read the following case study and answer the question that follows:

[Bharat Heavy Machinery: Functional Silos & Inter-Departmental Conflict]
Bharat Heavy Machinery Ltd (BHML) is a large engineering company in Bhopal producing customized thermal turbines.
The organization is structured strictly around key specialized enterprise functions:
- Production Department (supervised by Chief Production Engineer)
- Marketing & Sales Department (headed by Marketing Director)
- Finance & Accounts Department (headed by Financial Controller)
- Human Resource Management Department (headed by HR Director)
Each departmental head is a functional expert who exercises direct vertical authority over their respective team.
Recently, a delay in delivering a landmark turbine project to a state electricity utility triggered finger-pointing:
Production claimed Marketing gave unrealistic delivery dates without checking shop-floor inventory; Marketing alleged Production delayed assembly; and Finance withheld component import clearances due to currency volatility.
The General Manager observed: “Our functional silos are causing inter-departmental conflict and obscuring corporate goals.”

Question: Which type of organizational structure is demonstrated by Bharat Heavy Machinery Ltd?

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct analytical application of NCERT principle.

options.studentSelectionTrap: Divisional structure groups by products; BHML groups by enterprise functions.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Student error: Divisional structure groups by products; BHML groups by enterprise functions.

options.studentSelectionTrap: This is a formal administrative hierarchy.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Student error: This is a formal administrative hierarchy.
Student error: Not a matrix structure.

detailedSolution: Organizing the enterprise into major specialized departments based on functions (production, marketing, finance) is the definition of a Functional Structure.

solution.quick: Option (A) is correct: Functional Structure
solution.concept: Grouping jobs of similar nature under functions creates a Functional Structure.
solution.detailed: Organizing the enterprise into major specialized departments based on functions (production, marketing, finance) is the definition of a Functional Structure.

keyConcept: Bharat Heavy Machinery: Functional Silos & Inter-Departmental Conflict: Case Study Analysis

topic: Bharat Heavy Machinery: Functional Silos & Inter-Departmental Conflict
questionText:
Read the following case study and answer the question that follows:

[Bharat Heavy Machinery: Functional Silos & Inter-Departmental Conflict]
Bharat Heavy Machinery Ltd (BHML) is a large engineering company in Bhopal producing customized thermal turbines.
The organization is structured strictly around key specialized enterprise functions:
- Production Department (supervised by Chief Production Engineer)
- Marketing & Sales Department (headed by Marketing Director)
- Finance & Accounts Department (headed by Financial Controller)
- Human Resource Management Department (headed by HR Director)
Each departmental head is a functional expert who exercises direct vertical authority over their respective team.
Recently, a delay in delivering a landmark turbine project to a state electricity utility triggered finger-pointing:
Production claimed Marketing gave unrealistic delivery dates without checking shop-floor inventory; Marketing alleged Production delayed assembly; and Finance withheld component import clearances due to currency volatility.
The General Manager observed: “Our functional silos are causing inter-departmental conflict and obscuring corporate goals.”

Question: Why is it difficult to fix clear accountability for the delayed turbine delivery in BHML's functional structure?

options.text: Because government laws prohibit auditing functional departments.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Student error: Absurd distractor.

options.text: Because functional managers report solely to external trade unions.
options.studentSelectionTrap: Functional managers report to the General Manager.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Student error: Functional managers report to the General Manager.

options.text: Because engineering turbines requires zero managerial supervision.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Student error: Absurd distractor.

options.text: Because final performance depends on the collective contribution of multiple interdependent functional departments.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct analytical application of NCERT principle.

detailedSolution: Because product completion requires inputs from production, finance, and marketing jointly, no single department head can be held exclusively accountable for final delivery failure.

solution.quick: Option (D) is correct: Because final performance depends on the collective contribution of multiple interdependent functional departments.
solution.concept: Difficulty in fixing accountability is a core limitation of functional structure.
solution.detailed: Because product completion requires inputs from production, finance, and marketing jointly, no single department head can be held exclusively accountable for final delivery failure.
